lessons: Pick Tormented Pariah or Ashmouth Hound over a blue first pick like Claustrophobia, since Claustrophobia never made my WR deck and I had to settle for a fallback colour pair.
Draft more answers for green 4-toughness bodies: Somberwald Spider and Villagers of Estwald beat my red-white deck 2-0 in round 3.
My long wins and losses (35, 40, 30 turns) show that a red-white aggro deck with 17 lands and few evasive threats stalls, so prioritise flyers and cut a land for a low curve.

Don't run five Forests for four green cards: Elder of Laurels, Silverchase Fox and Unruly Mob strained my 12 Plains/5 Forest mana, and I drafted Spidery Grasp and Sensory Deprivation but played neither.
My two lost matches went 35, 40 and 56 turns, so favour evasive fliers and removal like Rebuke and Urgent Exorcism over extra Avacyn's Pilgrim mana accelerants that don't break stalls.
Settle the second colour by mid pack 2 rather than drifting: I ended with a light green splash of playables instead of a committed deck, and my 1-2 record reflected it.
Prioritise cheap removal like Dead Weight and Corpse Lunge over top-end: my UB deck had few early answers, and every match ran into long grinds of 15–25 turns.
Pick up cheap flying or reach blockers earlier: GW's three Chapel Geists and two Abbey Griffins flew over my ground Skaabs, Walking Corpse and Village Cannibals.
Blue-black was not the problem: seat 5 also drafted UB and went 2-1, so judge my deck by its interaction and curve, not its colours.
Mono-white with Fiend Hunter, Smite the Monstrous and Feeling of Dread went 2-1 against UB and WR but lost 0-2 to BG; keep a second colour's removal as insurance.
BG's Boneyard Wurm and Victim of Night outclassed my white board in both losses; keep a hedge colour's big bodies or removal as a backup.
Pack 1 picks 4 and 8, Night Terrors and Grimoire of the Dead, were wasted on colours I cut; settle on white sooner to get better two-drops.
Prioritise cheap removal: Brimstone Volley, Geistflame and Heretic's Punishment anchored this 2-1 RG deck, so take them over mid-curve creatures in the early picks.
Secure a second top-end threat: Essence of the Wild was RG's only real finisher, and the 51-turn game in the 1-2 loss to BG suggests stalled boards need more late power.
Value the 2-drops: Reckless Waif, Kruin Outlaw and the werewolves kept early pressure on, so keep that curve while weighing Kindercatch against Moonmist for the last slots.
Blue-black flyers (Moon Heron, Murder of Crows, Stitched Drake) plus Dead Weight and Victim of Night helped win 2-0 over UR and 2-1 over WG, including 25- and 56-turn games.
Ground-based RG beat me 1-2 in 16- to 17-turn games, so this slow deck needed more cheap early blockers and fewer expensive top-end cards.
Count your 40 before registering: my recorded list has 24 spells plus 17 lands, and still includes Disciple of Griselbrand despite the note to cut it.
Blasphemous Act, my pack 3 first pick, never reached my UR deck, so take first picks in the colours you will actually play.
My losses to UB ran 22 and 25 turns, suggesting my deck couldn't close stalled boards, so value finishers and fliers over extra ground filler.
Six red cards (Brimstone Volley, two Harvest Pyre, Pitchburn Devils, Riot Devils, Night Revelers) ran on only six Mountains, so give a split like that 8 or 9 red sources or cut red.
Green-black flowed here: Festerhide Boar, Villagers of Estwald, Kindercatch and removal Prey Upon, Victim of Night, Tribute to Hunger went 3-0 in matches.
Build the green-heavy costs with 10 Forest and 7 Swamp, and cut speculative off-colour cards like Avacyn's Pilgrim and Disciple of Griselbrand for 23 playables.
Expect grindy matches: Round 2 ran to a 51-turn game, so keep Boneyard Wurm and Morkrut Banshee's late-game value rather than chasing early speculative picks.
